newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Talebans release Argentine newsmen after beating.
newsitem.headline: Talebans release Argentine newsmen after beating.

text.p: Two Argentine television journalists were beaten and held for a day by Taleban Islamic fundamentalists who control Kabul, before being released Thursday, their channel and Argentine officials said.

Experienced war correspondent Natalio Aides and cameraman Walter Moor, both Argentine nationals, were detained by the new rulers of the Afghan capital Wednesday but released a day later thanks to U.N. mediation.

"They have been released. But we feared for their safety. They told us the Talebans beat them and took their camera away though they gave it back later," Ruben Saiegh, head of news at Argentine television channel Telefe, told Reuters.
"They were afraid they'd be taken to the Hotel Continental which the Talebans are using as a headquarters," he said.
An Argentine Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said the two journalists were awaiting the first available flight out of Kabul. "Apparently they are in good shape," she said.

Argentina's U.N. Ambassador Fernando Petrella said in letters to U.N. officials asking for help that the pair were "detained on charges of espionage". However Saiegh at Telefe said it was unclear why the Talebans had picked them up.

The Talebans have imposed stern Islamic Sharia law since taking over Kabul three weeks ago. They control three quarters of Afghanistan but the government they ousted is fighting back and ex-defence minister Ahmad Shah Masood has given them an ultimatum to quit the capital or face the consequences.
